Deepak: heads up — I found a perf regression on Mixtral-8B when head_dim is 48 (not multiple of 64 or 16) and we route to FlashAttention
Sara: ouch, what symptoms?
Mike: latency up or errors?
Deepak: latency. profiling shows the runtime is falling back to SDPA/Triton slower path. microbench: gen token p50 went from ~9.8ms to ~14.3ms after the model upgrade
Sara: any explicit warning in logs?
Deepak: yes — runtime prints: "kernel_select: flashattention incompatible (head_dim%8!=0), falling back to sdpa". also saw masked softmax differences for long contexts :eyes:
Eva: is this specific to Mixtral or we see it across Llama/Mistral/Qwen too?
Deepak: observed on Mixtral and a Qwen-7B variant with head_dim 56. Llama-2 variants with head_dim multiple-of-16 are fine
Mike: so head_dim odd multiples -> flashattn can't be used on current kernel. Is the fallback using our Triton SDPA or a plain cuBLAS matmul+softmax path?
Deepak: falls to our Triton SDPA path first; if Triton kernel build not available for that arch it goes to slow reference path (matmul + python masking)
Sara: how much perf hit if we force padding to multiple of 8 at runtime vs fixing kernels?
Deepak: quick test: padded KV tensors on-the-fly (pad head_dim to 64) -> p50 ~10.2ms. padding adds ~0.3ms overhead for copy but lets flashattn run
Mike: interesting. Any quality impact from padding? rope/scaling issues?
Deepak: none observed for short tests. BUT RoPE scaling edge-case: if we pad and don't adjust RoPE angle slicing, you must ensure the extra dims are zeroed and excluded from rotary indexing. I added a small clip in the RoPE kernel.
Sara: can we do a safer automatic padding + masking option in runtime kernel selector?
Deepak: prototype added: config flag `allow_headpad_for_flash = true` and `headpad_multiple = 8`. It pads within batch/kv allocation, applies zero mask for padded dims, and routes to flash
Mike: that sounds reasonable as a stopgap. Long term we should get FlashAttention/Triton kernels accepting any head dim (or implement unaligned kernels)
Eva: also need to check batching heuristics — padding interacts with batch concat. If small batches get padded a lot, unit token cost grows
Deepak: agreed. perf model shows padding cost amortizes past batch_size>=4. If single-token streaming, padding overhead dominates
Sara: any differences by GPU arch? A100 vs H100?
Deepak: H100 Flash kernels are stricter but faster; fallback penalties larger on H100 (because optimized flash path is much better). On older A100 the difference is smaller but still noticeable
Mike: what's the plan for rollout? slowpath acceptable until we patch Triton kernels?
Deepak: propose: 1) enable runtime head-pad flag for affected customers (opt-in) 2) add a kernel PR to accept head_dim % 8 != 0 for Triton/flash (working with upstream flashattention) 3) telemetry: add metric `kernel_fallback_reason=head_dim_misaligned`
Sara: please add an eval to ensure no softmax/masking correctness regressions. Also add a perf regression alert on route p50>12ms on stable models
Deepak: added quick eval harness: runs 100 prompts, checks token-by-token diff and logprob drift. no drift seen in padded runs. tests in: ```/mnt/runs/flare/flash-pad-check/176056*/report.txt``` 
infra-bot: deploy queued for canary to dedicated cluster-3 at 2026-02-05T14:22:00Z
Mike: good. who will own the Triton kernel PR?
Deepak: i'll open the PR but pinging @sara for review on integration with batcher and @eva for hw perf
Sara: ack, will review. can we log a short incident/notes in eng-runtime so oncall sees this pattern?
Deepak: created a short thread in incidents with timestamps and perf graphs. link: https://redwood.internal/incident/INC-2026-012
Mike: thanks. one more ask: add a fallback policy so routing can prefer model variants with head_dim multiples for latency-sensitive customers
Sara: good idea — policy config `prefer_aligned_models=true` per-customer
Deepak: will add config + unit tests. leaving notes in PR
Eva: final: add a small note in docs about RoPE edge-cases when runtime pads head dims
Deepak: done. pushing changes to testing stack now :thumbsup:
Mike: nice. follow up tomorrow after canary numbers
Sara: thanks all :rocket:
